paragraphs: He is mentioned in Gittin 67b: Rabbi Yohanan says in his name; and so it is in the Jerusalem Talmud there, at the end of chapter 6.[^1]

notes.text: The whole Davidson Gittin 67b paragraph explicitly has Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Elazar of Ruma, supporting the corresponding full local titles and reporting direction. The supplied רומא and digital רומה remain distinct. The Jerusalem Talmud end-of-chapter pointer is Hyman’s uncollated comparison, without a fresh cross-edition identity claim.
